subject: zoology
question_text: Give an account of glandular epithelium.

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya Junior Fastrack zoology section (book p.34, SAQ 23). Zoology holds only ONE source book — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only, and no zoology board paper is in the corpus — so the two-book union check and the back-test are both structurally impossible for this card; 'not checked' does NOT mean 'checked and clean'. The mark split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. BOOK WORDING: the book writes that glandular epithelium 'forms the covering of all major glands'. Glandular epithelium forms the SECRETORY part of a gland, not only its covering, and the card is written that way.

steps.label: What glandular epithelium is
steps.why: Every gland begins as an epithelium whose cells took up secretion, and that is why glands are studied under epithelial tissue at all.
common_mistakes: Writing that glandular epithelium only covers a gland. Its cells form the secretory part of the gland itself.
Calling it a connective tissue. It is an epithelial tissue.
steps.memory_tip: A gland is an epithelium that took up one job: secretion.
steps.margin_note: One sentence of definition and one line of function. The two classifications come next.

that forms the glands of the body.

steps.label: Classified by the number of cells
steps.why: The tissue is classified twice — once by how many cells make the gland, once by how the secretion leaves it — so the answer must keep the two classifications apart.
common_mistakes: Mixing the two classifications. Unicellular and multicellular is one pair; exocrine and endocrine is a different pair.
Giving no example. One example on each side is expected.
steps.memory_tip: One cell or many cells: a goblet cell against a salivary gland.
steps.margin_note: Two kinds with one example each. Keep this pair separate from the next.
lines: By the number of cells, glands are of two kinds.
cells. Example: goblet cells of the gut.

steps.label: Exocrine glands
steps.why: A duct is a tube, so an exocrine secretion can be delivered to one named place, which is why saliva reaches the mouth and milk reaches the outside.
common_mistakes: Writing that exocrine glands pour into the blood. Their duct carries the secretion out.
Naming the thyroid as exocrine. The thyroid is ductless, so it is endocrine.
steps.memory_tip: Exo means out, and the duct is the way out.
steps.margin_note: Duct, what it carries, two examples. Three lines.

steps.label: Endocrine glands
steps.why: With no duct the only route out is the blood, which is why a hormone reaches the whole body while saliva reaches only the mouth.
common_mistakes: Naming a duct for an endocrine gland. They are ductless, and that is the definition.
Calling the secretion an enzyme. Endocrine glands secrete hormones.
steps.memory_tip: No duct means only one road out: the blood.
steps.margin_note: The duct is the marked contrast. Close with two examples.
